The arrival of the Magyars, or Hungarians, in the Carpathian Basin around 895, which founded what became Hungary. Led by Árpád, seven allied tribes crossed the Carpathian passes from the steppes north of the Black Sea, after attacks by the Pechenegs and Bulgarians.

The Magyars spoke a Uralic language, unlike their Slavic and Germanic neighbours, and lived as horse herders and mounted archers. They took over a land held loosely by Great Moravia, the Bulgarians and the Franks, and destroyed Moravia in the early 900s.

For half a century Magyar horsemen raided deep into Western Europe, as far as Italy, France and Spain, until the German king Otto I beat them at the Battle of Lechfeld in 955. They then settled down. Their prince Stephen I was baptised and crowned the first king of Hungary in 1000 or 1001, bringing the country into Latin Christendom, as Poland had done a generation before.
